title: Nondegenerate cell presentation and subset embeddings of simplicial realization
statement: Let $K$ be a small simplicial set with geometric realization as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and let $q_\sigma:|\Delta^n|\to|K|$ be its continuous characteristic map for $\sigma\in K_n$. Every point of $|K|$ has a unique representative $(\sigma,t)$ with $\sigma$ nondegenerate and all barycentric coordinates of $t$ strictly positive; thus these images of simplex interiors are pairwise disjoint and cover $|K|$. Every simplex $\tau\in K_n$ is a degeneracy of a unique nondegenerate simplex $\sigma\in K_m$: there is an order-preserving surjection $\alpha:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[m]$ with $\tau=K(\alpha)(\sigma)$, and $q_\tau=q_\sigma\circ\alpha_*$, where $(\alpha_*t)_j=\sum_{\alpha(i)=j}t_i$. For every simplex $\rho\in K_n$ and every order-preserving map $\beta:[m]\to[n]$, the realization relation is $q_{K(\beta)(\rho)}=q_\rho\circ\beta_*$, where $(\beta_*t)_j=\sum_{\beta(i)=j}t_i$. A subset $B\subseteq|K|$ is closed if and only if $q_\tau^{-1}(B)$ is closed in $|\Delta^n|$ for every simplex $\tau\in K_n$. For a simplicial subset $A\subseteq K$, the inclusion-induced map $|A|\to|K|$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, and its image consists exactly of the points whose nondegenerate representative belongs to $A$. Here a simplicial subset is a family of subsets of $K_n$ stable under all face and degeneracy maps, and nondegenerate means not in the image of a degeneracy map.

proof.text: Let $Q:\coprod_{n,\tau\in K_n}|\Delta^n|\to|K|$ be the quotient map in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Its restriction $q_\tau$ to each summand is continuous. The generating quotient identification gives $q_{K(\beta)(\sigma)}(t)=q_\sigma(\beta_*t)$ for every monotone $\beta$, with exactly the coordinate sums in the statement. A subset $B$ of the quotient is closed exactly when $Q^{-1}(B)$ is closed, by applying the definition of the quotient topology to its complement. A subset of this disjoint union is closed exactly when its intersection with each summand is closed, by the definition of the disjoint-union topology. This proves the asserted closed-set criterion. The map $\beta_*$ is continuous because each of its finitely many coordinates is a finite sum of coordinates.

proof.text: For every simplex $\tau$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to obtain its unique nondegenerate ancestor $\sigma$ and surjection $\alpha$. Step 1 gives $q_\tau=q_\sigma\circ\alpha_*$. To normalize an arbitrary representative $(\tau,t)$ with $\tau\in K_n$, let $J=\{i:t_i>0\}$, enumerate it by the increasing injection $i_J:[r]\hookrightarrow[n]$, and let $u$ be the vector of its positive coordinates. The sum-one condition makes $J$ nonempty, $u\in|\Delta^r|$, and $t=(i_J)_*u$. Decompose $K(i_J)(\tau)=K(\alpha)(\sigma)$ by the cited node, with $\alpha:[r]\twoheadrightarrow[m]$ and $\sigma$ nondegenerate. The quotient relations give $(\tau,t)\sim(\sigma,\alpha_*u)$. Every coordinate of $\alpha_*u$ is strictly positive, since the corresponding fiber of the surjection is nonempty. Define this last pair to be the normal form of $(\tau,t)$; the uniqueness clause of the cited node makes this a well-defined function on representatives.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; agent expansion from unique nondegenerate decomposition to barycentric normal forms.

proof.text: We check that this normal form is unchanged by every generating relation $(K(\beta)(\tau),t)\sim(\tau,\beta_*t)$, where $\beta:[m]\to[n]$. Let $J\subseteq[m]$ be the positive support of $t$, let $H=\beta(J)\subseteq[n]$, and enumerate them by $i_J:[r]\hookrightarrow[m]$ and $i_H:[s]\hookrightarrow[n]$. Because all coordinates are nonnegative, the positive support of $\beta_*t$ is exactly $H$. There is a unique increasing surjection $\gamma:[r]\twoheadrightarrow[s]$ with $\beta i_J=i_H\gamma$: its value is the position in $H$ of $\beta(i_J(k))$. If $u$ is the positive-coordinate vector of $t$, the positive-coordinate vector of $\beta_*t$ is $v=\gamma_*u$. Decompose $K(i_H)(\tau)=K(\alpha)(\sigma)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition]. Functoriality gives $K(i_J)K(\beta)(\tau)=K(\alpha\gamma)(\sigma)$. The composite $\alpha\gamma$ is surjective and $\sigma$ is nondegenerate, so uniqueness in the cited node says this is exactly the decomposition used to normalize the left side. Its normal form is $(\sigma,(\alpha\gamma)_*u)$; that of the right side is $(\sigma,\alpha_*v)$. They coincide, since in each coordinate both sums are $\sum_{k:\alpha(\gamma(k))=j}u_k$. Thus normal forms are invariant under a generating relation, its reverse, and finite chains of them, hence descend to the equivalence classes of the realization quotient.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; agent expansion from unique nondegenerate decomposition to barycentric normal forms.

proof.text: A representative $(\sigma,t)$ already having $\sigma$ nondegenerate and $t$ strictly positive is its own normal form: its support injection is the identity, and its unique decomposition is the identity surjection with ancestor $\sigma$. Every representative is equivalent to its normal form by step 2. If two such nondegenerate interior representatives determine the same realization point, step 3 makes their normal forms equal, hence they are the same pair. This proves existence and uniqueness, and therefore the disjoint covering by nondegenerate simplex interiors.

proof.text: Let $A\subseteq K$ be a simplicial subset. For any $z\in A_n$, decompose $z=K(\alpha)(\sigma)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition]. Choose an increasing section $s:[m]\to[n]$ of $\alpha$ by taking the least element in each fiber; the fibers are consecutive nonempty intervals, so $s$ is increasing. Then $\sigma=K(s)(z)\in A_m$. Thus a simplex of $A$ is nondegenerate in $A$ if and only if it is nondegenerate in $K$, and its unique decomposition and its barycentric normal form are the same in both simplicial sets. Consequently the realization map $e:|A|\to|K|$ is injective and its image is exactly the points whose nondegenerate representative belongs to $A$. This map is continuous: by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] its composite with the quotient map presenting $|A|$ is $q_z$ on each simplex summand $z\in A_n$, hence continuous; the defining quotient topology implies continuity of $e$.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; agent expansion from unique nondegenerate decomposition to barycentric normal forms.

proof.text: To prove that $e$ is closed, fix any closed $C\subseteq|A|$ and put $B=e(C)$. We prove by strong induction on $n$ that $q_\tau^{-1}(B)$ is closed for every $\tau\in K_n$. If $\tau\in A_n$, the equation $q_\tau=e\circ q^A_\tau$ and injectivity of $e$ give $q_\tau^{-1}(B)=(q^A_\tau)^{-1}(C)$, which is closed. If $\tau$ is degenerate, [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] writes $\tau=K(\alpha)(\sigma)$ with $\dim\sigma<n$ (a surjective endomorphism of $[n]$ is the identity). Step 1 gives $q_\tau^{-1}(B)=\alpha_*^{-1}(q_\sigma^{-1}(B))$, closed by induction and continuity of the coordinate sums. Finally suppose $\tau$ is nondegenerate and outside $A_n$. By steps 4 and 5, its simplex interior maps outside $e(|A|)$, so $q_\tau^{-1}(B)$ lies in the boundary. For $n=0$ that boundary is empty. For $n>0$, on the closed face $F_i=\{t_i=0\}$, the insertion-of-zero map $(\delta_i)_*:|\Delta^{n-1}|\to F_i$ is a homeomorphism with inverse deleting that coordinate, and $q_\tau\circ(\delta_i)_*=q_{K(\delta_i)(\tau)}$. Induction makes the inverse image on each face closed in that face, hence in the whole simplex because $F_i$ is closed. Their finite union is exactly $q_\tau^{-1}(B)$ and is closed. This completes the induction. The quotient closed-set criterion of step 1, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], now shows that $B$ is closed in $|K|$.

proof.text: Taking $C=|A|$ in step 6 shows that $Y=e(|A|)$ is closed in $|K|$. The continuous injective map of step 5, corestricted to $Y$ with its subspace topology, is a continuous bijection $|A|\to Y$. For each closed $C\subseteq|A|$, step 6 makes $e(C)$ closed in $|K|$ and hence in $Y$. Thus the inverse bijection is continuous by the closed-set criterion for continuity, and the corestriction is a homeomorphism. Its image description is step 5. This includes $A=\varnothing$ and $A=K$.

lean.statement: theorem realization_cw_subcomplex (K : SSet.{u}) : (∀ x : |K|, ∃! (p : Σ n : ℕ, {σ : K _⦋n⦌ // σ ∈ K.nonDegenerate n} × {t : |SSet.stdSimplex.obj ⦋n⦌| // realizationInterior t}), (realizationCharacteristic p.2.1.val) p.2.2.val = x) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (τ : K _⦋n⦌), ∃! (p : Σ m : ℕ, Σ α : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌, K _⦋m⦌), Function.Surjective p.2.1.toOrderHom ∧ p.2.2 ∈ K.nonDegenerate p.1 ∧ τ = K.map p.2.1.op p.2.2) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (τ : K _⦋n⦌) (m : ℕ) (α : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌) (σ : K _⦋m⦌), τ = K.map α.op σ → realizationCharacteristic τ = realizationCharacteristic σ ∘ realizationBarycentricMap α) ∧ (∀ (n m : ℕ) (α : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌) (t : |SSet.stdSimplex.obj ⦋n⦌|) (j : Fin (m + 1)), (⦋m⦌.toTopHomeo (realizationBarycentricMap α t)) j = ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), if α.toOrderHom i = j then (⦋n⦌.toTopHomeo t) i else 0) ∧ (∀ (n m : ℕ) (ρ : K _⦋n⦌) (β : ⦋m⦌ ⟶ ⦋n⦌), realizationCharacteristic (K.map β.op ρ) = realizationCharacteristic ρ ∘ realizationBarycentricMap β) ∧ (∀ B : Set |K|, IsClosed B ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ) (τ : K _⦋n⦌), IsClosed ((realizationCharacteristic τ) ⁻¹' B)) ∧ (∀ A : K.Subcomplex, ∃ e : |A.toSSet| ⟶ |K|, e = SSet.toTop.map A.ι ∧ Topology.IsClosedEmbedding e ∧ (∀ x : |K|, x ∈ Set.range e ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (σ : A.toSSet _⦋n⦌), σ.1 ∈ K.nonDegenerate n ∧ ∃ t : |SSet.stdSimplex.obj ⦋n⦌|, realizationInterior t ∧ realizationCharacteristic σ.1 t = x))
lean.note: The helper declarations give the canonical characteristic and barycentric maps and interior predicate; the theorem states the nondegenerate representative, degeneracy, coordinate, quotient-topology, and simplicial-subcomplex clauses.
